\[
\begin{gathered}
G_x = K_x \star I, \qquad G_y = K_y \star I,
\\[4pt]
\lvert \nabla I \rvert_2 = \sqrt{G_x^2 + G_y^2}, \qquad
\lvert \nabla I \rvert_1 = \lvert G_x \rvert + \lvert G_y \rvert, \qquad
\theta = \operatorname{atan2}(G_y,\, G_x)
\end{gathered}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(I\): Input values. Luma by default.
- \(K_x,\ K_y\): The horizontal and vertical Sobel kernels shown in the Operator tab
- \(\star\): Correlation. The kernel is applied without flipping.
- \(G_x,\ G_y\): Horizontal and vertical change at each pixel
- \(\lvert \nabla I \rvert\): Gradient magnitude, which is the edge strength
- \(\theta\): Gradient direction in radians, measured from the x axis toward the y axis. The y axis points down.

K_x responds to changes from left to right and K_y to changes from top to bottom. Each kernel takes a difference across the edge and a 1, 2, 1 weighted average along it. G_x and G_y are linear filters. The magnitude and the direction combine them in a nonlinear way.
